newsitem.title: USA: Chubb taking bids for New Hampshire unit.
newsitem.headline: Chubb taking bids for New Hampshire unit.

text.p: Chubb Corp announced it is formally accepting offers for its Chubb LifeAmerica life insurance subsidiary.
Chubb LifeAmerica President Theresa Stone explained the decision in a letter to employees distributed late on Monday.

"Indeed, the response from potential buyers has been so strong that everyone involved has reached the same conclusion: The most immediate value for the company is likely to be realized through its sale. Therefore Chubb has decided to solicit formal offers for Chubb Life," the letter said.
Chubb, a Warren, N.J., firm specializing in casualty and property insurance, warned employees of Chubb LifeAmerica two months ago that low earnings was forcing the parent company to consider a sale.

Industry observers believe Chubb will seek a mutual fund or bank to buy the Concord-based subsidiary, which was founded in the 19th century as United Life and Accident Insurance Co. and has some 750 employees.
Stone apologized to employees for raising uncertainty during the holidays and promised more news about the company's future in January.

Concord city officials were viewing the sale and possible relocation of the company with gloom. Chubb LifeAmerica is the city's top employer and has donated millions of dollars to community projects ranging from an arts theater to affordable housing.
